maria (runtime): FYI I ran an end-to-end profile on the latest runtime build and we have a troubling tail-latency bump when long-history requests hit the new fused-attn kernels. p95 up ~8%, p99 up ~18% in the 2-8k token window. Anyone else seeing this?

jason (perf): I saw the same in our nightly perf job. Repro is stable on A100 and H100. The kernel change reduces avg token latency for short contexts but introduces variance for long KV cache walks.

lee (infra): Can you paste the perf traces? which stage is spiking — kernel, memcpy, or sync? :thinking:

maria (runtime): Trace snippet: ```stage:token_gen kernel_ms:0.72 memcpy_ms:0.18 kv_lookup_ms:1.35 wait_ms:0.40 total_ms:2.65``` The kv_lookup_ms is the main diff vs baseline (was ~0.45ms).

sophia (ml): Looks like the fused-attn kernel changed the memory access pattern for KV cache offsets. For long histories the scatter/gather cost dominates.

jason (perf): TL;DR: Kernel selection heuristics currently favor lower-avg latency kernels but ignore long-tail access costs. We should add a tail-aware score: score = avg_latency + alpha * p99_latency_component.

maria (runtime): Agreed. Also want to discuss microbatch sizing and max_tokens caps as temporary mitigations. Options: 1) adaptive microbatch that reduces batch size for requests with >N cached tokens, 2) per-request soft cap on max_tokens for requests with long context, 3) server-side truncation policy or graceful reject.

lee (infra): From an infra POV, adding a short-term max_tokens cap is low-risk. We can implement a default 512 token cap for requests where context_size + requested_tokens > 4096 and bump via account flag.

jason (perf): For batching heuristics, propose: microbatch_size = clamp(1, floor(target_tokens / avg_seq_len), max_microbatch), where target_tokens is tuned for p95 target. Example: target_tokens=4096 gives smaller microbatches for long sequences.

sophia (ml): We should ensure kv cache eviction/truncation semantics are consistent: if we truncate history server-side we must update the KV pointers correctly and avoid a full cache rebuild on the next token. Suggest implement pointer-shift truncation (O(1)) + tombstone TTL for stale rows.

maria (runtime): Good point. We also hit a perf regression in the profiler where repeated small microbatches cause scheduler thrash. We might want to introduce a microbatch coalescing window: coalesce for up to 5ms or until N requests queued. Tradeoff adds a tiny latency but lowers p99.

lee (infra): Ops-bot suggests a rollout plan: enable soft max_tokens caps and coalescing in canary (10% traffic) with metrics: p50/p95/p99, kernel-specific tail, and request_reject_rate. ops-bot: "deploy scheduled: canary 10% at 02:00 UTC"

ops-bot: deploy started: runtime-canary-v18 -> canary-10% (watch: 01:30 UTC).

jason (perf): Also add a profiling probe to record per-request kernel choice and kv_hit_pattern. Minimal schema: `{kernel, context_len, requested_tokens, microbatch_size, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, kv_walk_ms}`. Put that into our perf index so we can correlate kernel vs tail.

maria (runtime): For timeouts: propose default soft_timeout=2500ms, hard_timeout=4500ms for generation endpoints. Soft timeout triggers early token trim and returns partial result + reason code. Hard timeout aborts and returns 504+diagnostics. Thoughts?

sophia (ml): Soft timeout + partial outputs is user-friendly. We need to include continuity token so clients can resume from KV state if they retry. Also set policy: if truncated due to timeout, mark example in evals to check quality impact.

lee (infra): We'll need to expose the timeout and max_tokens caps in the API response headers so customers can tune: `x-rw-timeout`, `x-rw-truncated`, `x-rw-kv-start`.

jason (perf): Another mitigation: fallback to quantized/low-memory kernel variant for requests where context_len>threshold. This reduces KV pressure at cost of slightly higher avg per-token compute but often less tail variance.

maria (runtime): Action items: 1) jason: add tail-aware kernel scoring and perf probe (ETA: 2d). 2) sophia: define KV pointer-truncation semantics + resume token spec (ETA: 3d). 3) lee: implement soft max_tokens cap and coalescing window in canary (ETA: 1d). 4) ops-bot: run canary and collect p50/p95/p99 (start time planned).

sophia (ml): I'll also add a small eval suite: 1000 long-history prompts to validate quality under truncation/timeouts. We'll flag regressions >2% quality drop.

lee (infra): Quick config snippet for canary I'm going to push: ```yaml microbatching: coalesce_window_ms: 5 max_microbatch: 32 target_tokens: 4096 adaptive: true timeouts: soft_ms: 2500 hard_ms: 4500 max_tokens_policy: {default_cap: 512, long_context_threshold: 4096, allow_override_tier: enterprise}```

maria (runtime): Thanks. If canary looks stable we'll roll to 50% and then GA. Keep the perf traces coming — the kernel maintainers need concrete p99 correlations to tune the fused-attn path. :thumbsup:

jason (perf): I'll post the perf index query once it's live. For immediate monitoring add an alert: p99 > baseline*1.15 for 10min -> rollback canary.

ops-bot: canary metrics link: https://perf.internal/runs/20230401/canary-v18

lee (infra): Noted. Will enable alert and watch memory fragmentation on GPU too.

maria (runtime): Great runbook. Closing loop: we'll treat max_tokens cap + coalescing as short-term protective measures while we fix kernel selection and KV access pattern. Followups in a dedicated doc. Thanks all.
